outcome.summary_plain: You get a small link shortener you run on your own machine or a VPS. You paste a long link into a page, optionally give it your own short name, and get back a short link you can share. Opening a short link sends the visitor straight to the original page and quietly counts the visit. The same page lists all your links with how many times each was opened and when it was last used.

you_will_see.what: The dark 'Tool' page: a one-row form with a long-link field, an optional name field and a Shorten button; below it two big counters for total links and total opens; then a table of code, target, opens, last open and copy.
A green confirmation line with the new short link after a successful shorten, and a red line with a readable reason when the address is not valid or the custom name is already taken.

you_will_see.where: A short link in any browser or with curl
you_will_see.what: An immediate redirect to the original address; the open count for that link goes up by one on the page.
A plain 'Not found' page instead of a redirect.
`npm test` runs the full test suite covering shortening, redirects, counting and validation, and exits cleanly.

stays_the_same: The look and layout are exactly the 'Tool' sketch you approved; nothing about the design is being reconsidered.
The light 'friendly' alternative design is removed, along with the /_alt address that served it during the sketch.
There is still no login: anyone who can reach the port can create links and see the list.
There is no way to delete or edit a link, and the list shows every link on one page without paging.
to_see_it: Run `npm install` once, then `npm start`, and open http://localhost:8080
Needs Node 24 or newer (your machine has 26.7)

open_questions.question: Your brief says Node 22+, but the built-in SQLite the sketch uses is only stable from Node 24 onwards. Require Node 24+, or add the better-sqlite3 package so Node 22 keeps working?
open_questions.proposed_answer: Require Node 24 or newer and record that in the project manifest. Your machine runs 26.7, and this keeps the promise of zero runtime dependencies.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The alternative adds a native dependency that has to be compiled on every machine you deploy to, which is the opposite of the 'minimal dependencies' constraint.

open_questions.question: If you put this on a VPS, should creating links and viewing the list require a secret, or is the whole thing open to anyone who finds the address?
open_questions.proposed_answer: Leave it open, as the sketch had it. Redirects must stay public in any case.
open_questions.why_it_matters: An open shortener on a public VPS lets strangers hide their own links behind your domain. Adding a secret later changes how you call it and how the page works.

scope.reason: A new, empty repository: three small endpoints, one static page and a SQLite data layer, all shown working in the agreed sketch. Nothing existing changes, and the look is fixed by the sketch the owner picked.

process.why: Small, low-risk job (S): one phase, one review at the end.

phases.title: The shortener, built properly and covered by tests
phases.goalPlain: After this phase you can run the app, shorten a link on the page, open the short link, and watch the open count rise — with a test suite proving all of it.

handoff.summary_plain: The shortener works end-to-end: you can paste a URL on the dark 'Tool' page (matching the approved sketch exactly), optionally give it a custom name, get a short link back, and opening that link redirects immediately while the open count and 'last opened' time update on the page. Unknown codes show a plain 'Not found' page. Codes are cryptographically random and effectively unguessable. The light 'friendly' design and its /_alt route were removed as agreed, there's still no login, and no delete/edit/pagination was added — all as planned. The full automated test suite passes. The only thing not literally watched in a browser is the green/red confirmation message on the form, which was verified by reading the code and testing the API directly instead of a live screenshot.

delivered.promise: Shorten links: POST a URL, get a short code, optional custom alias, URL validation
delivered.note: Validates http/https only, alias pattern-checked and race-safe 409 on collision

delivered.promise: Redirect: GET /:code returns 302 to the original URL; 404 for unknown codes
delivered.note: Indexed lookup; click recording failure can't block the redirect (tested)

delivered.note: GET /api/links returns clicks + lastClickAt, computed in SQL

how_to_see: Run `npm install` then `npm start` in the project directory
Open http://localhost:8080 in a browser — shorten a URL, note the short link
Open the short link in a new tab, confirm it redirects, then reload the main page and see the open count and 'last open' time update
Try a bogus code like http://localhost:8080/zzzzzzz to see the 'Not found' page
Run `npm test` to see the full suite pass
known_gaps: The form's success/error message was verified by code reading and direct API calls, not a live screenshot, due to a headless-browser cross-origin limitation. Low risk; worth a 30-second manual check.
